checks.result: source-consistent
checks.detail: Compute input uses interactive quality and validates width 24...192, divisible by 3, before computing height or allocating pixel storage. Height is width * 2 / 3, so maximum output is 192 * 128 * 4 = 98,304 bytes and dimension conversions fit UInt32. Scene validation bounds lights to 12. Interactive rectangular lights contribute at most 64 samples each, making 768 samples / 2,304 float4 rows / 36,864 sample bytes. Areas contribute at most 36 float4 rows / 576 bytes, and parameters contain six float4 rows / 96 bytes. These are payload bounds inferred from source, not device memory measurements.

checks.result: source-consistent
checks.detail: Host indices 0...4 match shader parameters/samples/areas/output/dimensions. Swift SIMD4<Float> rows and shader float4 rows are consistent; three rows are produced and consumed per sample and per area. Empty sample/area buffers bind one zero row while shader counts remain zero. Output uchar4 indexing matches four bytes per pixel; dimensions use SIMD2<UInt32>/uint2.

checks.result: source-consistent
checks.detail: Positive group width is bounded by pipeline maximum threads. Group height is at least one and capped by both eight and maximumThreads/groupWidth, keeping the product within the pipeline limit. Rounded-up X/Y group counts cover all validated pixels. Shader rejects either out-of-range gid component before writing rgba[gid.y * width + gid.x], so excess edge threads cannot write outside the output buffer.
